_readme: Moving between provincial schools and national schools - the official position.
SOURCING RULE FOR THIS PAGE: official .gov.lk sources only, linked and never copied.
WHAT WAS NOT FOUND, and why the page says so plainly: no circular on the Ministry's
own index covers teacher movement between national and provincial schools. The NSTT
portal is transfers WITHIN national schools; the provincial pages are INTER-PROVINCIAL
transfers. Do not fill that gap with a procedure from a news site or a Facebook group -
teachers act on this, and a wrong step costs them a year. Re-check the sources above
and update the dates before editing.

pages.title: Moving Between Provincial and National Schools
pages.metaTitle: Provincial to National School Transfers for Teachers | RCF English
pages.description: How teacher transfers work between provincial schools and national schools in Sri Lanka: who administers each system, which officers an application goes through, and what the Ministry has and has not published.
pages.keywords: national school transfer, provincial school transfer, teacher transfer Sri Lanka

hero.text: The two systems are run by different authorities, which is why this is not an ordinary transfer. What follows is what the official sources actually say - and where they say nothing.

blocks.title: Read this before you plan anything around it
text: This page is a **guide to the official sources**, not an authority in itself. RCF English cannot transfer anyone, and nothing here overrides a circular or an instruction from your Zonal or Provincial Director.

Everything below was checked on **5 October 2026** against the Ministry of Education and provincial ministry websites. Transfer rules change with each circular, so confirm the current position before you act on it.
**Get the answer in writing.** A verbal assurance from any office is worth nothing if a later officer disagrees with it.

blocks.heading: Why this is not an ordinary transfer
text: A transfer within one system moves you between schools under the *same* authority. Moving between a provincial school and a national school does not do that - it crosses from one appointing authority to another, and that is a different kind of move altogether.

**National schools** are administered directly by the Ministry of Education. **Provincial schools** are administered by the Provincial Ministry or Department of Education, and provincial transfers are recommended to the **Provincial Public Service Commission**.

So a move between them is not simply a longer transfer. One authority has to release you and the other has to take you on. That is why you will not find a single form for it in the place you would expect, and why teachers lose months looking for one.

blocks.heading: What the official sources do say
intro: Three official sources carry the published detail. None of them is about moving between the two systems, which is the point - but each tells you something you need.

items.q: The National School Teacher Transfer portal
a: This handles transfers **within national schools**. Applications are made online, and the portal states that **no amendment is possible once an application is submitted** - so everything is checked before it goes.
It also sets a compulsory threshold: a teacher must apply where the service period at the current school reaches **eight years or more** by the end of the year in question.
The round is annual. The 2026 window closed on **30 July 2026**, so if you are reading this afterwards, watch the portal for the next call rather than assuming it is still open.

The portal publishes notices and instructions in Sinhala, Tamil and English, transfer criteria, medical certificate formats and the national schools list. It carries **nothing** about provincial schools.

Provincial ministries publish the chain an application travels: teacher, then **principal**, then **Zonal Director of Education**, then **Provincial Director of Education**, then the Provincial Ministry, which recommends to the Provincial Public Service Commission.

The Southern Provincial Ministry lists these documents for an inter-provincial transfer: the **application**, a **certified copy of the letter of appointment**, the **original regarding audit queries and disciplinary action**, and a **certified copy of the letter of service confirmation**.

That list is for transfers **between provinces**. Treat it as a guide to the kind of paperwork your own province will want, not as the list for a move to a national school - and confirm it with your own Provincial Ministry, since provinces differ.

The Ministry publishes its circulars, with Sinhala, Tamil and English versions. As checked on 5 October 2026, the transfer circulars listed there cover the **Sri Lanka Teacher Educators' Service** and the **Sri Lanka Education Administrative Service**, and there are separate circulars for the Principal Service.

A **National Teacher Transfer Policy** exists and has been reported as intended to balance teacher distribution between national and provincial schools. If movement between the two is opened to you, it will be under an instrument of that kind - which is why the circulars index is the page worth watching.

blocks.title: What is not published - said plainly
text: As at 5 October 2026, **no circular on the Ministry's own index sets out a procedure for a teacher moving between a national school and a provincial school in either direction.** The national portal covers national schools; the provincial pages cover provinces.

That absence is worth knowing, because the usual advice online fills it in with detail from news sites and teachers' groups. Some of that may be accurate. None of it is authority, and acting on it can cost you a transfer cycle - a year.
If someone shows you a document that does set out this procedure, it will have a **circular number and a date**. Ask for those two things. Anything without them is hearsay.

blocks.heading: What to do instead
intro: Since there is no published route, the practical approach is to put the question to the people who must answer it, in a form they have to answer in writing.

items.title: Start with your own chain of command
text: Your principal, then your Zonal Director of Education. They handle transfers constantly and will know whether anyone in your zone has made this move recently, and under what instrument.
Going around them does not work and does not help you: a transfer file travels through these officers whatever route it eventually takes.

items.title: Ask in writing, and ask a precise question
text: Not *can I move to a national school*, which invites a shrug. Ask: **under which circular may a teacher of the Sri Lanka Teachers' Service attached to a provincial school be released to a national school, and which authority approves it?**
A question naming a circular has to be answered with a circular, or with an admission that there is not one. Either answer is useful.

items.title: Put the same question to the Teacher Transfer Unit
text: The Ministry's transfer office is the other half of the answer, because it is the receiving authority. The National School Teacher Transfer portal published the numbers **011 278 4434** and **011 207 5854** as at 5 October 2026.
Ask them for the circular number. Write down who you spoke to and when.

items.title: Watch the circulars index, not social media
text: If this route opens properly, it will appear as a numbered circular on the Ministry's own circulars page, in all three languages. That page is the first place it will be true.
Teachers' groups will have it first and will have it slightly wrong. Use them to know that something has happened, then go and read the circular.

items.title: Keep every document certified and ready
text: Whatever route opens, the paperwork will be the same family: letter of appointment, service confirmation, and a clear record on audit queries and disciplinary action.
Getting certified copies takes time you will not have once a window opens. Hold them ready.
